# Smarter Compact [![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/smarter-compact.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/smarter-compact) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Apache_2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![GitHub](https://img.shields.io/badge/github-bcmyguest%2Fsmarter--compact-blue)](https://github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact) **Context management (smart compaction) for coding agents.** Long sessions keep small, cached prompts. Every message goes into a local SQLite session store. Once the prompt reaches your token limit, older turns leave it, and the next kept turn carries a pointer to them.

The agent searches the store with `smart_compact_search`, `smart_compact_sql`, and `smart_compact_get` when it needs a detail back. The cut stays put on later requests, so the prompt cache keeps hitting. **Learn more:** [How it works](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/context-management/) · [Benchmarks](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/benchmarks/) · [Context proxy & port](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/context-proxy/) · [Context store](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/context-store/) **Benchmarks:** On [ContextBench](https://github.com/RulinShao/ContextBench) ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37725), [dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/context-language-model/ContextBench)) with Haiku 5.5, smart compaction cost 85% less than keeping everything, averaged over four task sizes (v0.9.0, 2026-11-09). [Tables and charts](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/benchmarks/) · [Methods and caveats](https://bcmyguest.github.io/smarter-compact/context-research/#deviations-from-the-pre-registration).

Trimmed context is marked with a `[smarter-compact: …]` pointer. You need Node 24 or newer (for `node:sqlite`). Agents that trim through the proxy also need LiteLLM `1.109.0rc1` (pinned) on `PATH` as `litellm`. `smarter-compact enable` installs it with `uv tool install` when it is missing or another version. Without uv, it stops and changes no agent config. The plugin has no API key of its own. Your agent keeps its own login. ### How agents integrate Smart compaction needs something that **sees and rewrites the model request** before it is sent: a proxy or an in-process hook. | Tier | Agents | What you get | | --- | --- | --- | | **Full trim (proxy)** | Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode 1 | `smarter-compact enable` points the CLI at the loopback LiteLLM proxy; every turn is stored and older turns drop off the wire at the token threshold. | | **Full trim (in-process)** | OpenCode 2, Pi | JS port of the trim core in the agent's **`context` hook**; includes prose strip, observation masking and the progress note ([OpenCode plugin](docs/opencode.md), [Pi extension](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions#context) in this package). No proxy URL. | Cursor and Copilot CLI get hooks and MCP search tools only, with no automatic trim. See [Optional: Cursor and Copilot](#optional-cursor-and-copilot). ## Install Install from npm with `npm install -g smarter-compact`, then register plugins with **`smarter-compact plugins add `**. It finds the installed package itself, so you need neither `npm root -g` nor a git clone. **`smarter-compact enable -g`** detects Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode (by config dir, or `opencode` on PATH), points each at the proxy, and starts the proxy. It prints each step to stderr; `-q` (or `SMARTER_COMPACT_QUIET=1`) prints only errors and warnings. Clone the repo only to develop the trimmer or to pin a checkout path. ### Claude Code ```sh npm install -g smarter-compact smarter-compact plugins add claude smarter-compact enable claude ``` Start a new `claude` session after `enable`. The marketplace install registers the search tools and the compact command. `enable` points `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at `http://127.0.0.1:4101`, starts the LiteLLM proxy in the background when needed, and stores a key in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env` (mode 600). Session hooks also ensure the proxy is up. `enable` saves any previous base URL in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy-backup.json`, and `smarter-compact disable claude` restores it. Logs: `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.log`. Set `SMARTER_COMPACT_AUTO_PROXY=0` to disable auto-start. **Remote Control.** Claude Code refuses [Remote Control](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/remote-control) while `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points anywhere but `api.anthropic.com` ("Remote Control is only available when using Claude via api.anthropic.com"). The `env` block in `~/.claude/settings.json` overrides the shell, so `unset` does not help. Run `smarter-compact disable claude` before `claude remote-control` or `/remote-control`, and `smarter-compact enable claude` afterwards. Sessions started while disabled bypass the proxy and are not trimmed. On Claude Code 2.1.275 or later you can install the plugin from inside Claude Code instead of running `plugins add`: ``` /plugin install smarter-compact --marketplace bcmyguest/smarter-compact ``` That adds the search tools, hooks and commands. Trimming still needs `smarter-compact enable claude`, which points Claude Code at the proxy.
Optional: install from a git clone ```sh git clone https://github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact.git cd smarter-compact ./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact plugins add claude ./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact enable claude ``` Leave the clone in place; Claude resolves the marketplace from that path.
### Codex ```sh npm install -g smarter-compact smarter-compact plugins add codex smarter-compact enable codex ``` `enable` sets `model_provider = "smarter-compact"` in `~/.codex/config.toml`. Codex keeps its ChatGPT login: the provider uses `requires_openai_auth` and LiteLLM's `/backend-api/codex` pass-through. Trust the hooks, quit Codex, and start it again.
Optional: install from a git clone ```sh git clone https://github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact.git cd smarter-compact ./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact plugins add codex ./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact enable codex ```
### Pi ```sh pi install git:github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact ``` Pi loads `plugin/pi/smarter-compact.js`, which registers on Pi's **`context` hook** (documented on [pi.dev](https://pi.dev/docs/latest/extensions#context)) and runs the same in-process trim as OpenCode 2. Configure thresholds with `smarter-compact context set …` or `~/.config/smarter-compact/config.toml`. Command: `/smarter-compact compact` forces a trim on the next request.
Optional: git clone (local extension path) ```sh git clone https://github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact.git # Point Pi at smarter-compact/plugin/pi/smarter-compact.js per Pi's local-extension docs. ```
### OpenCode ```sh npm install -g smarter-compact opencode plugin smarter-compact # project .opencode/opencode.json opencode plugin -g smarter-compact # global ~/.config/opencode/ ``` **OpenCode 2** trims in the plugin (`context` hook). Add options on the plugin entry if you need them; see [docs/opencode.md](docs/opencode.md). **OpenCode 1** has no context hook, so run `smarter-compact enable opencode` as well (the plugin starts the proxy when the agent is pointed at it). `enable opencode` refuses a proxy base URL when `opencode --version` reports major 2.
Optional: install from a git clone ```sh git clone https://github.com/bcmyguest/smarter-compact.git cd smarter-compact opencode plugin "$PWD" # or ./index.mjs if your OpenCode build accepts a file path opencode plugin -g "$PWD" smarter-compact enable opencode # OpenCode 1 only ```
## Upgrade Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode 1 send requests through the background proxy, which keeps running the version that started it. OpenCode 2 and Pi trim in-process and pick up the new version on their next start. ```sh npm install -g smarter-compact@latest smarter-compact proxy restart # load the new proxy now claude plugin marketplace update smarter-compact # Claude Code: refresh the plugin, claude plugin update smarter-compact@smarter-compact # then restart claude ``` Skip `proxy restart` and the next session start restarts the proxy once it has been idle 60 s, showing `proxy restarted, -> `. A proxy that is busy, or that `smarter-compact` did not start, gets a warning naming what to restart instead. `proxy restart` stops only a litellm that `smarter-compact` started, or a Docker container publishing the port; it works on Linux, macOS and Windows. See [Updates](docs/context-proxy.md#updates) for the rules. ## CLI After `npm install -g smarter-compact`, the command on your PATH is **`smarter-compact`**. From a clone, use `./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact` (or `node plugin/scripts/smarter-compact.mjs`). ## Commands | Command | Effect | | --- | --- | | `/smarter-compact:status` | Trims, tokens saved (pre-trim estimate minus the billed prompt after the cut), and fail-opens in the last day | | `/smarter-compact:compact` | Trim on the next request. The hook writes `sessions/.force` | | `smarter-compact plugins add ` | Add the bundled plugin marketplace to that CLI (Copilot: MCP only — no trim) | | `smarter-compact path` | Print the installed package root (for custom scripts) | | `smarter-compact enable -g` | Detect Claude/Codex/OpenCode and point each at the proxy | | `smarter-compact install cursor` | Optional: MCP + hooks for Cursor Agent (no automatic trim) | | `smarter-compact enable ` | Point one agent at the proxy | | `smarter-compact disable ` | Remove that pointing and restore the backup | | `smarter-compact proxy` | Run LiteLLM in the foreground (debugging; hooks normally start it detached) | | `smarter-compact proxy restart` | Stop the background proxy and start a fresh one, e.g. after an upgrade (Linux, macOS, Windows) | | `smarter-compact status` | Same numbers as the slash command | A fail-open sends the request on untrimmed and records the error, so a failed trim never blocks a request. ## Where state lives `SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR` defaults to `~/.local/share/smarter-compact` for smarter-compact and the plugin. The store is `$SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR/context`. Schema and file layout: [docs/context-store.md](docs/context-store.md). Every setting and default: [configuration reference](docs/configuration.md). ### Proxy port Default is **4101**. To use another port: ```sh export CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=4200 smarter-compact enable claude # agent URLs and proxy.env both use 4200 ``` Or set it once in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env` (same file as the LiteLLM key), then run `smarter-compact enable` again so agent configs pick up the port. The hook and auto-started proxy also read every proxy setting (`PROXY_ENV_CONTEXT_KEYS` in `plugin/lib/brand.mjs`) from that file when they are not already in the environment: ``` CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=4200 # Per-model thresholds (config.toml — preferred): # smarter-compact context set haiku=95000 # smarter-compact context set default=125000 # Global override for every model: # smarter-compact context set trim=120000 # Or uncomment: # CONTEXT_TRIM_AT_TOKENS=120000 ``` The OpenCode 2 `proxyPort` option sets the port that plugin probes; it starts a proxy there only when an agent config already points at that port. Other agents read `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT`. ## Tests ``` python3 -m unittest discover -s proxy/tests node --test tests/plugin.test.mjs ``` The Python package is still `smarter_compact`. `plugin/lib/context-trim.mjs` is the OpenCode port of that package; the two stay on the same store contract. ### Optional: Cursor and Copilot These agents expose **MCP and session hooks only**. They do not rewrite model traffic, so **context is not trimmed automatically**. Use them if you want `smart_compact_*` tools and session registration while you work in Claude, Codex, OpenCode, or Pi for long sessions. **Copilot CLI:** `smarter-compact plugins add copilot` after the npm install. **Cursor Agent:** `smarter-compact install cursor`, reload Cursor, enable the local plugin. `enable -g` does not install Cursor unless you set `SMARTER_COMPACT_INSTALL_CURSOR=1`. ## Developing (git clone) ```sh npm ci npm test ./setup_prek.sh # prek hooks: file hygiene + Conventional Commits on commit-msg ``` The docs site (Astro Starlight) builds from `docs/*.md`: `cd site && pnpm install && pnpm test && pnpm build` writes `site/dist/` and fails on a broken link. CI runs the same `prek run --all-files` plus `npm test` and proxy unit tests, and `npm test` again on `windows-latest`. Tests that delete a home holding session databases must call `rmHome` from `tests/rm-home.mjs`, because Windows cannot delete an open file. Use `feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, etc. so **Prepare release** can bump semver with git-cliff. ## Releases Version bumps follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) via [git-cliff](https://git-cliff.org/) (`cliff.toml`). On `main`, run the **Prepare release** GitHub Action (dry-run first if you want the proposed version and notes). It bumps `package.json` (`npm version` copies the version into the plugin manifests; `npm run pack:check` fails if they differ), tags `vX.Y.Z`, and dispatches **Release** (tests, npm publish, GitHub Release body from git-cliff). Locally: `git-cliff --bumped-version` and `git-cliff --unreleased --strip header`. ## License Apache-2.0. The trimmer comes from [openmem](https://github.com/bcmyguest/openmem).

# How it works Context management (smart compaction) keeps long coding-agent sessions under a token limit without an LLM summary. Every message goes into a local SQLite session store. Older turns leave the context, and the next kept turn carries a pointer to them. The agent searches the store when it needs a detail back.


Older turns move to the session store, the cut turn carries a pointer, and smart_compact_search pulls a detail back.

Each request goes through these steps ([context proxy](context-proxy.md) has implementation detail): | Step | When | Effect | | --- | --- | --- | | Tool-result compression | A tool result exceeds `compress_over_tokens` | First 40 and last 20 lines stay, behind a `smart_compact_get(id=...)` header; the full text goes to `blobs/.txt` | | Store | Every request | Each message goes into `sessions/.db` once, keyed by a chained fingerprint, with an `in_context` flag ([context store](context-store.md#session-database)) | | Trim | The request reaches `trim_at_tokens`, or the user typed `/smarter-compact:compact` | Turns before the last real user turn, and the oldest tool exchanges of a long in-flight turn, leave the context and their rows get `in_context = 0`; a pointer naming `smart_compact_search` / `smart_compact_sql` replaces them. System prompt, tools, the first user turn, the reply before the last user turn, that turn and at least its last 3 tool exchanges stay verbatim, except that signed thinking leaves every kept assistant message but the latest ([why](context-store.md#trim)) | | [Tool-result clearing and masking](clearing.md) (on by default) | Part of each trim | Every tool result but the 10 newest, and the results in the kept turns before the latest run, become a short placeholder; the calls stay, and each result stays in the store | | [Lifecycle eviction](eviction.md) (off by default; `CONTEXT_EVICTION=1`, proxy) | Every 3 assistant steps, instead of the trim | Old tool results the rules mark unneeded (a file read or written again later, a command re-run, a result nothing later refers to) become the same placeholder; the threshold trim does not run, the agent's own compaction stays the overflow guard | | [Scratchpad](scratchpad.md) (on by default; `CONTEXT_SCRATCHPAD=0` turns it off) | The prompt passes `CONTEXT_SCRATCHPAD_NUDGE_AT` of the threshold, then the next trim | One nudge, attached to the newest user or tool message ([note placement](context-store.md#note-placement)), asks the agent to create the pad once (goal, status, decisions, facts, next step) with `smart_compact_scratchpad` and to update it only on a big change; every trim note opens with the current pad (≤2,500 chars) in a `` block labelled possibly stale, and snapshots it | | Standing instruction | Every request | A constant system-prompt note tells the agent to call `smart_compact_search` before relying on content it cannot see | The cut is **sticky**: later requests with the same history get the same rewrite byte for byte, so the prompt cache keeps hitting. A trim invalidates the cache once. ## Benchmarks ContextBench quality, time, cost and prompt-cache results: [Benchmarks](benchmarks.md). ## When to use it | Turn it on when | Leave it off when | | --- | --- | | Sessions grow past `trim_at_tokens` (default 125k estimated tokens, 95k for Haiku) | Sessions stay under the limit | | You want trimmed turns searchable, not summarized away | You cannot run `litellm` on the host (Claude, OpenCode 1, Codex point at the proxy) | | You use Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode 2, or Pi | You only need MCP search hooks on Cursor or Copilot (no automatic trim) | ## Turn it on ```sh smarter-compact enable claude # or codex, opencode (OpenCode 1) ``` The plugin **starts the LiteLLM proxy in the background** when an agent is pointed at it. OpenCode 2 trims in-process: `opencode plugin smarter-compact` — no proxy URL. Force a trim in session: `/smarter-compact:compact` (or agent equivalent). Status: `smarter-compact status` or MCP `context_status`. ## Agent support Which agents trim on the wire, which trim in-process, and which get search tools only: [Agents](agents.md). ## MCP tools | Tool | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `smart_compact_search` | FTS / hybrid search over trimmed session rows | | `smart_compact_sql` | Read-only SQL on one session database | | `smart_compact_get` | Text of a compressed tool result by blob id, `BLOB_PAGE_CHARS` (12,000) per call; returned as one header line (`[smart_compact_get id=…: characters 0-12000 of N; next page: offset=12000]`) then the raw text, not JSON; `offset` pages, `max_chars` (≤100,000) asks for more at once | | `context_status` | Trims, fail-opens, writer versions, usage summary | | `smart_compact_scratchpad` | Unless `CONTEXT_SCRATCHPAD=0`: `view`, `create`, `str_replace`, `insert` on the session's pad, capped at 2,500 characters | Wire format and SQL rules: [context store](context-store.md). ## Configuration Every setting, its default and the component that reads it: [configuration reference](configuration.md#trim). ## More - [Tool-result clearing and masking](clearing.md) — what a trim replaces instead of deleting turns - [Lifecycle eviction](eviction.md) — rule-based eviction every batch, instead of the threshold trim - [Scratchpad](scratchpad.md) — the agent's notes, shown in every trim note - [Context proxy](context-proxy.md) — LiteLLM rewrite pipeline - [Context store](context-store.md) — schema, trim rules, search tools - [OpenCode](opencode.md) — plugin install - [Configuration](configuration.md) — every setting and default - [Context research](context-research.md) — related work, run notes, and benchmark method

# Context proxy

For Claude Code, OpenCode 1, and Codex, **Smarter Compact** runs a local **LiteLLM** process (`smarter-compact proxy`, or auto-started by the plugin) that rewrites each request before forwarding to the real model API:

1. **Tool-result compression.** Results over `CONTEXT_COMPRESS_OVER_TOKENS` become a short header plus `smart_compact_get(id=...)`; full text in `blobs/<id>.txt`.
2. **Store.** Messages go into `sessions/<sid>.db` ([session database](context-store.md#session-database)).
3. **Trim.** At `CONTEXT_TRIM_AT_TOKENS` or when `sessions/<sid>.force` exists, older turns drop from the request; dropped rows get `in_context = 0`; a pointer replaces them at the start of the kept turn.
4. **Standing instruction.** Every request gets a constant system note to use `smart_compact_search` before guessing about trimmed content.

The cut is sticky for prompt-cache stability. **OpenCode 2** applies the same rules in-process (`plugin/lib/context-trim.mjs`); it does not send traffic through this proxy.

Code: `proxy/smarter_compact/`, `proxy/smarter_compact_hook.py`, `proxy/config.yaml`. Tests: `python3 -m unittest discover -s proxy/tests`.

You need **LiteLLM 1.109.0rc1** (pinned; the first release candidate with PR #41522) on `PATH` as `litellm` for Codex ChatGPT pass-through. `smarter-compact enable` checks `litellm --version` and, when it is missing or another version, runs `uv tool install --force 'litellm[proxy]==1.109.0rc1'`. Without uv it stops before it changes any agent config; run the proxy with `docker compose` from a clone instead (see `compose.yaml`). Session hooks only start the proxy; they never install.

## Proxy port

Default listen port is **4101** on `127.0.0.1`.

| Mechanism | Precedence |
| --- | --- |
| `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT` environment variable | wins |
| `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=` in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env` | used when env unset |
| Built-in default | `4101` |

Change port before or during enable:

```sh
export CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=4200
smarter-compact enable claude
```

Or add `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=4200` to `proxy.env`, then run `smarter-compact enable` again so agent URLs match.

The OpenCode 2 `proxyPort` option sets the port that plugin probes; it starts a proxy there only when an agent config already points at that port. Other agents read `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT`.

Auto-start is off when `SMARTER_COMPACT_AUTO_PROXY=0`. Logs: `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.log`, rotated to `proxy.log.1` at 5 MB on each start.

## Configuration

Every proxy setting, its default and which settings OpenCode 2 also reads: [configuration reference](configuration.md#trim).

Secrets: `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env` (mode 600), created by `smarter-compact enable`.

## Server-side tool-result clearing

`CONTEXT_SERVER_CLEAR=1` (off by default) asks Anthropic to clear old tool results on its side ([context editing](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/context-editing)). On the Anthropic route (`/v1/messages`) to a model whose id contains `claude`, the proxy appends one edit to the request body:

```json
{"context_management": {"edits": [{"type": "clear_tool_uses_20250919",
  "trigger": {"type": "input_tokens", "value": 100000},
  "keep": {"type": "tool_uses", "value": 3},
  "clear_at_least": {"type": "input_tokens", "value": 5000}}]}}
```

- **Merge, not replace.** Claude Code already sends `context_management` on its requests, `{"edits": [{"type": "clear_thinking_20251015", "keep": "all"}]}` on all 25,310 requests that carried the field in 400 Terminal-Bench Claude Code transcripts (`keep: "all"` clears nothing); no `clear_tool_uses` edit appeared. The proxy appends after the client's edits (the API wants `clear_thinking` first) and leaves a request that already carries a `clear_tool_uses_20250919` edit unchanged.
- **Beta header.** LiteLLM's Anthropic messages transform adds `context-management-2025-06-27` to `anthropic-beta` for a body with `context_management` (`litellm/llms/anthropic/messages/native/transformation.py`).
- **`clear_at_least` is the cache-break gate.** Clearing rewrites the prompt from the first cleared result, so the cached prefix after that point is written again. The edit applies only when it frees at least this many input tokens; otherwise the request goes up uncleared and the cache stays warm.
- **The store keeps everything.** The session store records the client's request before any edit is applied upstream, so cleared results stay searchable with `smart_compact_search` / `smart_compact_sql`.
- **Logged per call.** Each `usage` [event](context-store.md#events) gets `applied_edits`: the response's `context_management.applied_edits` as compact JSON (`[]` when nothing cleared, `NULL` when not reported). For a stream, it comes from the final `message_delta`; with the flag on, the hook reads the tail of each stream for it, passing chunks through unchanged.

Live check, 2026-11-05: Claude Code 2.1.318 `claude -p` on `claude-haiku-5-5` through a proxy from this tree (trigger 20000, keep 1, clear_at_least 1000), four `seq` tool calls: five requests, all `200`, the last two recorded `[{"cleared_input_tokens":1518,"cleared_tool_uses":2,"type":"clear_tool_uses_20250919"}]` and `cleared_input_tokens` 1526, cache reads stayed 42,989 and 44,432 tokens on those calls, and the store held all four tool results. Cost $0.16.

## Prompt-cache timing

Both settings are off by default and need the request clock: with either on, the trim state records per thread root the last request's arrival (`last_request`: epoch seconds `at`, idle gaps over 5 minutes `long`). Anthropic's [prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching) docs: "Cache write tokens with a 5-minute TTL are 1.25 times the base input tokens price", "with a 1-hour TTL are 2 times", reads 0.1; "The lifetime is measured from the start of the request that writes or reads the cache entry"; "a 1-hour cache entry must appear before any 5-minute cache entries".

**Cold-cache trim** (`CONTEXT_COLD_TRIM=1`, proxy and OpenCode 2). When the gap since the thread's previous request exceeds the cache lifetime, the request rewrites its whole prefix anyway, so it runs the normal trim to the target although the prompt is under the threshold: only when the estimate is above the target and the trim frees at least `CONTEXT_COLD_TRIM_MIN_GAIN_TOKENS` (default 5000; `CONTEXT_TRIM_MIN_GAIN_TOKENS` when larger). The lifetime: on the Anthropic route, 3600 s when a message `cache_control` (or the top-level one) has `ttl` `"1h"`, 300 s for other markers (also when the TTL split below sends `"5m"`); otherwise `CONTEXT_COLD_TRIM_SECONDS` (default 3600; OpenAI's `in_memory` retention lasts "up to one hour", its `24h` retention longer). The OpenCode 2 plugin never sees `cache_control`, so it always uses `CONTEXT_COLD_TRIM_SECONDS`. The `trim` event has `location` `cold`.

**Split cache TTL** (`CONTEXT_CACHE_TTL_SPLIT=N`, proxy Anthropic route only, including Bedrock and Vertex models behind it). When tools or system carry a `"1h"` marker, every message marker's `ttl` `"1h"` goes up as `"5m"`, so each turn's new content is written at 1.25× instead of 2×, while tools and system stay cached for an hour. No breakpoint is added or moved. After a gap over 5 minutes the conversation entry has expired and the request writes everything after the system prompt again at 1.25×. From the thread's Nth such gap on, the proxy sends the client's markers unchanged, so the switch happens once, on a request whose tail is cold anyway. Every request before it gets the same decision. The OpenAI and Chat routes and the plugin ignore the setting. `usage` events record `cache_creation_1h_tokens` and `cache_creation_5m_tokens` from Anthropic's `usage.cache_creation`.

## Token estimate

The trim uses a **calibrated estimate** from provider usage:

1. Pre-call hook counts request characters and keys them by `litellm_call_id`. Tools with `defer_loading: true` are left out: they cost no prompt tokens until loaded, and Claude Code sends hundreds of KB of them. The encrypted payloads of thinking blocks (`thinking.signature`, `redacted_thinking.data`) count at face value with `CONTEXT_STRIP_OLD_REASONING` on (the default): on Haiku 5.5 a thinking block kept in a tool loop bills one token per 3.1 to 3.3 signature characters ([measured](context-store.md#signed-reasoning)), close to text. With it `0` they are left out, as before. The thinking text itself counts.
2. Success hook records `{chars, tokens}` per conversation thread in `.trim.json`.
3. The next request in the thread extrapolates with the observed chars/token ratio (bounded 1–8).

The estimate only decides **whether** to cut; it does not change an existing sticky cut.

## Enable

```sh
npm install -g smarter-compact   # or clone this repo
smarter-compact enable claude                 # writes settings + starts proxy if needed
```

Claude Code (`~/.claude/settings.json`):

  "env": {
    "ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL": "http://127.0.0.1:4101",
    "ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS": "x-litellm-api-key: Bearer <LITELLM_MASTER_KEY>"
  }
}
```

Replace `4101` with your `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT`. Do not put `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` in the proxy environment; the client’s own credentials pass through.

## Debug request shapes

Set `CONTEXT_DEBUG_SHAPES=1` (environment or `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env`) and restart the proxy. Each request then writes one line to `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.log`, as received from the client: item count, pinned items, system prompt size in characters, tool count, the thread root fingerprint and the roles of the last 12 items. It logs counts only, never message content. Use it to tell whether a short request left the client short or was cut in the proxy.

## Run it in Docker (from this repo)

`compose.yaml` at the repo root runs the same proxy without installing LiteLLM: it starts the pinned LiteLLM image with `./proxy` mounted at `/app/proxy`, so **the requests are rewritten by the code in this checkout** — `docker compose restart context-proxy` is the deploy step.

```sh
HOST_UID=$(id -u) HOST_GID=$(id -g) docker compose up -d context-proxy   # or put both in ./.env
docker compose logs -f context-proxy
```

It needs `LITELLM_MASTER_KEY` in `~/.config/smarter-compact/proxy.env` (mode 600; `CONTEXT_PROXY_ENV_FILE` overrides the path), listens on `127.0.0.1:${CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT:-4100}`, and writes the session store to `~/.local/share/smarter-compact/context` — falling back to the deprecated openmem service's `~/.local/share/openmem/context` when only that exists, so switching which repo serves it changes no agent config and orphans no session a running agent can still recall. Set `CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT=4101` to move onto the CLI default instead.

## Updates

The proxy writes `proxy-<port>.json` to the context dir at start, and at most every 5 s while it serves requests: its `package.json` version, pid, start time and last request. At each session start (and on `smarter-compact enable`), the plugin compares that version with the installed package:

| Proxy on the port | Idle 60 s or more | Busy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Started by the plugin (`proxy.pid`, same pid as the status file) | Stopped and started from the installed package | Warning |
| Docker compose container whose checkout's `package.json` matches the installed version | `docker restart <container>` | Warning |
| Compose container on another checkout version, a manual `smarter-compact proxy`, or no status file | Warning | Warning |

Claude Code and Codex show the warning as a session-start system message; `enable` prints it to stderr. A warning names what to restart or update.

`smarter-compact proxy restart` restarts at once. It stops only the litellm in `proxy.pid` (checked to be litellm; on Windows with its child processes) or a Docker container publishing the port, refuses any other listener, then starts the installed version.

## Limits

- **One LiteLLM worker.** Session locking is in-process; do not run multiple workers.
- **Fail open.** Rewrite errors log one line and forward the request untrimmed; `fail_open` events in the session DB.
- **Codex pass-through** requires the dev LiteLLM build noted above.
- **No Claude Code Remote Control.** Claude Code blocks Remote Control while `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at the proxy; run `smarter-compact disable claude` first ([quick start](quick-start.md#claude-code)).
- **OpenAI-format clients** need explicit routes in `proxy/config.yaml` unless using Anthropic models (see comments in that file).

# Context store contract

This file is the context-store contract for **Smarter Compact**. The Python package is `proxy/smarter_compact`; the JavaScript port is `plugin/lib/`. `SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR` defaults to `~/.local/share/smarter-compact`; files live under `$SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR/context`. Wire text (`[smarter-compact: …]`, `smart_compact_*`) matches OpenMem for compatibility.

See [how it works](context-management.md) and [context proxy & port](context-proxy.md).

The context proxy, the OpenCode plugin (which trims in-process), and the `smart_compact_*` MCP tools exchange state through local files. Below, "proxy" means whichever of the two trims a session. This page is the contract between them; change it before changing any side.

## Location

Root: `$SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR/context`, default `~/.local/share/smarter-compact/context` (`~/.local/share/openmem/context` is still used when it exists and the new one does not). Surrounding ASCII whitespace (space, `\t`, `\n`, `\v`, `\f`, `\r`) is trimmed from `SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR`; an empty value after trimming means the default. Directories are mode 700, files mode 600. The context-proxy container bind-mounts this directory read-write and runs as the host UID/GID.

| Path | Writer | Reader | Content |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions/<sid>.json` | SessionStart hook, OpenCode plugins | proxy, MCP | Registration: `{"session_id", "agent", "cwd", "registered_at"}` (ISO 8601 UTC) |
| `sessions/<sid>.force` | prompt hook or OpenCode plugin on `/smarter-compact` | proxy | Empty flag. The proxy trims on the next request for that session, then deletes the flag. |
| `sessions/<sid>.trim.json` | proxy | proxy | Proxy-private trim state (cut point, fingerprints, reported-usage samples for the token estimate, see [context-proxy.md](context-proxy.md#token-estimate)). Other components must not depend on its shape. |
| `sessions/<sid>.db` (+ `-wal`, `-shm`) | proxy | MCP `smart_compact_search`, `smart_compact_sql`, shell `sqlite3` | [Session database](#session-database): every message of the session, in or out of context. The only store of record for message content. |
| `blobs/<id>.txt` | proxy, OpenCode 2 plugin | MCP `smart_compact_get` | Full text of a compressed or [cleared](clearing.md) tool result, served back in 12,000-char pages. `id` = first 16 hex chars of SHA-256 of the UTF-8 content. |
| `scratchpad/<sid>.md` | MCP `smart_compact_scratchpad` | proxy | The agent's pad (unless `CONTEXT_SCRATCHPAD=0`). Every trim copies it, capped at 2,500 characters, into the start of the note under a possibly-stale label, keeps the file, and saves a snapshot `<sid>.<n>.md` (n the next free integer). |
| `tool-calls.jsonl` | MCP `smart_compact_*` tools | `smarter-compact context stats` | One JSON line per search / sql / get call (`at`, `tool`, hit/row/char counts). Best-effort telemetry; not part of the session rewrite contract. Moves to `tool-calls.jsonl.1` at 5 MB, replacing the previous generation; stats read both. |
| `.ttl-stamp` | proxy, MCP server | proxy, MCP server | Empty; its mtime records the last [retention](#retention) sweep |

Earlier releases wrote `sessions/<sid>.log.jsonl` handoff logs. Nothing writes or reads them now and they are not migrated; the retention sweep deletes them with their session.

## Session id

`<sid>` is the agent's session id after this rule, applied identically by the hooks and plugins (`sanitizeSessionId` in `cli/coding-agent/context-store.mjs`), the proxy (`sanitize_sid` in `proxy/smarter_compact/store.py`) and the MCP tools:

1. Trim surrounding ASCII whitespace (space, `\t`, `\n`, `\v`, `\f`, `\r`); other whitespace is not trimmed.
2. Replace every Unicode code point outside `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` with one `_` (`😀` becomes `_`, not `__`).
3. Reject an empty result: hooks write no file, the proxy tries the next source below, the MCP tools return an error.

Dots are kept, so `..` survives (`ses/../x` becomes `ses_.._x`). That is safe because step 2 removes every path separator and each file name appends a suffix (`.json`, `.db`, ...), so no sid names a path outside `sessions/`. Registration and trimming accept such ids. The MCP tools additionally reject an explicit `session_id` argument that contains `/` or `\`, or that is `.` or `..`; pointers always give the agent the sanitized id, which never has a separator.

The proxy takes the first non-empty id, in order, from:

1. the `x-smarter-compact-session-id` request header (sent by Smarter Compact's OpenCode plugin through its `chat.headers` hook);
2. the `x-claude-code-session-id` header (Claude Code; equals the hook `session_id`);
3. `metadata.user_id` JSON `session_id`, then the legacy `user_id` form ending in `_session_<id>` (8 or more of `[0-9A-Za-z-]`); the request's own `metadata` first, then `proxy_server_request.body.metadata`;
4. `prompt_cache_key` (Codex sends its conversation id there), from the request then from the original body;
5. the `session_id`, `x-session-id` and `conversation_id` headers, in that order.

Sources 3 (legacy form), 4 and 5 cover clients Smarter Compact does not wire yet; only Claude Code and OpenCode are wired. When no source yields an id, the proxy uses `fp-<first 16 hex of SHA-256(system prompt + first user message)>`; such sessions have no registration, but trimming still works.

## Trim

A trim keeps, in their original order:

- pinned messages before the cut (Anthropic `system` messages, which Claude Code uses for its environment, model id and deferred-tool list; Chat and Responses `system` / `developer` messages; OpenCode 2 `system` messages). Pinned messages are not written to the store;
- the **first real user turn**, verbatim: Anthropic, the first `user` message that is not only `tool_result` blocks; Chat, the first `user` message; Responses, the first user `message` item; OpenCode 2, the first `user` message that is not only `tool-result` parts. It usually states the task, so every trim keeps it ahead of the pointer;
- the **reply before the cut**: the agent message just before the cut turn, when it is a final reply (an assistant message with no tool calls; Responses, a `message` item), so the cut turn reads as an answer to it;
- the cut turn, carrying the pointer note ([note placement](#note-placement));
- everything after the cut turn except the **in-turn gap**.

A trim runs when the `.force` flag exists or the request's estimated prompt tokens reach the threshold. The estimate is calibrated from the provider's reported usage, with `CONTEXT_CHARS_PER_TOKEN` (default 2.5) as the fallback ratio ([context-proxy.md](context-proxy.md#token-estimate)); it never moves an existing cut.

The cut is the last real user turn after the previous cut whose kept part shares no tool call/result pair with the dropped part. When no such turn drops anything (for example, while the first user turn is still in flight), the cut is the existing cut, else the last real user turn.

The in-turn gap drops the oldest tool exchanges of the cut turn's own agent loop, so one long prompt can still be trimmed. A step is one tool exchange: Anthropic, Chat and OpenCode 2, an assistant message and the results after it; Responses, a `reasoning` item, or a call or reply not preceded by reasoning or a call, and what follows it. The tail after the gap keeps the newest 3 steps, then older steps while the request stays under `CONTEXT_TRIM_TO_TOKENS` (default `haiku` 50000, else 66000; capped at the trim threshold); the step right after the cut turn is never kept in the tail, and a step is never split. A turn with 3 steps or fewer has no gap. Later trims of the same cut only move the gap forward; a new cut starts a new gap. The cut and gap are stored with fingerprints, so later requests render the same bytes until the next trim.

### Signed reasoning

A trimmed view drops **signed reasoning** from every kept assistant message before the latest assistant message at trim time (with `CONTEXT_STRIP_OLD_REASONING=0`, before the latest assistant run: the trailing run of assistant items ending at the last one); that message goes out unchanged. A Responses `reasoning` item and the calls after it count as one message. The trim records where it starts as `strip` / `strip_fp` in the thread state, next to `cut` and `gap`. With `CONTEXT_CLEAR_KEEP_RESULTS` on it also records `clear` / `clear_fp`, the first message whose tool results stay whole; every kept result before it renders as its mask placeholder (`[smarter-compact: tool output cleared to save context; smart_compact_get(id="<id>") returns it]`, the id of a blob holding its text) until a later trim moves the bound forward. A thinking signature covers the whole prefix before it, and the trim edits that prefix (dropped messages, the pointer), so a kept older block would no longer verify; Anthropic's API rejects it, and LiteLLM hides the 400 by retrying with all thinking removed. (Three probes on 2026-11-08, `claude-haiku-5-5` with adaptive thinking, a Claude Code tool loop of four assistant steps: thinking on the last step only, the same with a middle step dropped, and thinking kept on the first and last but not the third; all three returned `200`.) What counts as signed, per format:

| Format | Removed from older kept assistant messages | Kept |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Anthropic | `thinking` and `redacted_thinking` content blocks | everything else |
| Chat Completions | LiteLLM's `thinking_blocks` field (the signed Anthropic blocks) | `reasoning_content`, unsigned text that LiteLLM sends again only through `thinking_blocks` |
| Responses | `reasoning` items whose `encrypted_content` is LiteLLM's encoding of signed Anthropic thinking | OpenAI `reasoning` items: their encrypted content is not tied to the earlier messages |
| OpenCode 2 | `reasoning` parts carrying a signature (`encrypted`, or `providerMetadata.<provider>.signature` / `redactedData`) | unsigned reasoning parts and OpenAI `reasoningEncryptedContent` |

With `CONTEXT_STRIP_OLD_REASONING` on, a message that would be left with no content keeps its reasoning, so stripping never drops or empties a message; a Responses `reasoning` item is reasoning, not a message, and goes. With it `0`, such a message is dropped; it held only reasoning, so no tool call/result pair is split. Reasoning produced after the trim was generated on the trimmed view and stays, so the rendered prefix is byte-identical from one request to the next until the next trim moves `strip`. (Stripping each former latest message as newer ones arrived changed the prefix on every turn that thought and re-wrote the trimmed history to the prompt cache.) Untrimmed requests keep every block.

Only signed Anthropic reasoning is stripped. The other formats keep their reasoning because their providers need it in the tool loop: DeepSeek returns `400` when `reasoning_content` is missing from a request with `tools` ([thinking mode](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/thinking_mode/): "for requests carrying the tools parameter, the reasoning_content must be fully passed back to the API in all subsequent requests"); Gemini returns `400` when the current turn's first `functionCall` lacks its thought signature ([thought signatures](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/thought-signatures)); OpenAI asks for every reasoning item in order ([reasoning, keeping reasoning items in context](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning#keeping-reasoning-items-in-context)); OpenRouter `reasoning_details` must match the model's output. Anthropic requires only the turn in progress: "Required: within a tool-use turn, pass thinking blocks back. Recommended: across turns, pass everything back. Allowed: outside tool use, omit prior turns' thinking" ([preserving thinking blocks](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#preserving-thinking-blocks)); the probes above show the API accepts a tool loop with thinking on its last step only.

With `CONTEXT_STRIP_OLD_REASONING` on, estimates charge signature characters at face value. Measured on four `tb21-h55-clearfit` trials (Claude Code, Haiku 5.5): `count_tokens` returns the same count with and without the thinking blocks, so it does not see them, but billed usage minus `count_tokens` of the same request without thinking (less a constant 3,754-token offset seen before any thinking) gives the thinking cost:

| Trial | Request (of the first trim) | Billed prompt | Thinking | Share | Signature chars per token |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| adaptive-rejection-sampler | 6 | 98,631 | 64,124 | 65% | 3.12 |
| regex-chess | 5 | 93,242 | 68,442 | 73% | 3.30 |
| make-mips-interpreter | 15 | 87,581 | 42,299 | 48% | 3.08 |
| make-doom-for-mips | 20 | 90,831 | about 37,000 | about 41% | about 3.25 |

At 2.3 to 3 characters per text token, face value overstates thinking by at most about 30%.

### Batched reasoning strip (`CONTEXT_STRIP_REASONING_EVERY`)

Off by default (`0`). Without a trim, every earlier thinking block stays in the request. With `N` > 0, when a request opens a new batch of N assistant steps (assistant items, as [eviction](eviction.md) counts them), the proxy and the OpenCode 2 / Pi plugin may move a recorded reasoning bound forward to the latest assistant message. They strip signed reasoning from every assistant message before it by the rules above: Anthropic `thinking` / `redacted_thinking`, Chat `thinking_blocks`, signed plugin `reasoning` parts. A message holding only reasoning keeps it, and every turn stays. A Responses `reasoning` item is left whole here, because dropping an item would shift the indices the trim state records. The bound moves only when the strip frees at least `CONTEXT_STRIP_REASONING_MIN_TOKENS` (default `8000`) estimated tokens, signatures charged at face value; otherwise it waits for the next batch. Each move rewrites the prompt cache from the first stripped block: 1-hour cache writes bill at 2× input, reads at 0.1×. On Claude 5.1+ models an edit before a kept thinking block makes the API drop that block (`input_transformations: thinking_dropped, prefix_binding_mismatch`), and the model thinks again, so moves stay rare. The bound only moves forward and is recorded in the thread state (`reason`, `reason_fp`, and `reason_batch`, the last batch checked), carried through trims. Requests between moves render the same bytes. The strip shrinks the estimate, so the threshold trim fires later; a trim also counts what the bound already took off. Each move writes a `strip_batch` [event](#events) (`tokens_before`, `tokens_after`).

Offline replay of `tb21-h55-idevict` and `tb21-h55-rtk` (96 main transcripts, Claude Code with Haiku 5.5): each request goes through the proxy (trim at 95,000, target 40,000, clearing 10, `CONTEXT_STRIP_OLD_REASONING=1`), billed as text characters over the trial's fitted ratio plus signature characters ÷ 3.2, with that usage fed back. Cache model: a request reads the longest message prefix byte-identical to the previous request's view and writes the rest. Relative cost = 2.0 × write + 0.1 × read (Haiku 5.5 ratios; uncached input is 1× but every byte here is cached or written; output and thinking-drop re-thinks not modelled):

| N / floor | Trims per trial | Dropped messages per trial | Strip moves per trial | Cache-write tokens per trial | Billed input tokens per trial | Relative cost per trial | vs off |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| off | 0.98 | 19.2 | 0 | 125,706 | 1,606,852 | 399,526 | — |
| 6 / 4,000 | 0.53 | 9.9 | 3.19 | 149,324 | 1,394,889 | 423,204 | +5.9% |
| 6 / 8,000 | 0.54 | 9.9 | 2.27 | 146,820 | 1,421,700 | 421,127 | +5.4% |
| 12 / 4,000 | 0.67 | 10.6 | 1.85 | 145,721 | 1,491,162 | 425,987 | +6.6% |
| 12 / 8,000 | 0.68 | 10.9 | 1.40 | 142,975 | 1,512,946 | 422,947 | +5.9% |
| 24 / 4,000 | 0.79 | 14.6 | 0.79 | 135,275 | 1,535,852 | 410,608 | +2.8% |
| 24 / 8,000 | 0.80 | 14.6 | 0.66 | 134,175 | 1,538,040 | 408,736 | +2.3% |

Every arm cuts trims by 18% to 46%, dropped messages by 24% to 48% and billed input by 4% to 13%. Every arm also costs more, because cache writes rise more than reads fall. The 8,000 floor beats 4,000 at every N, hence its default. N = 6 removes the most trims, N = 24 costs least, and N = 12 is dominated by N = 6 on both. The setting stays `0` until a benchmark arm measures pass rate against that cost;
…[文件过长——仅保留首 16KB 与末 8KB]…
: …] pointer. Removed content is saved, not forgotten. When you need earlier content you cannot see in your context — values, ids, keys, counts, decisions — call smart_compact_search (use `pattern` for exact ids/keys, `context` for neighbouring rows; `line_matches` gives exact counts) or smart_compact_sql for counts and aggregates over the session store; never guess from memory you cannot see. This trim never summarizes removed content — a remembered "summary of earlier context" is not its record; cite a search result instead.
Don't repeat work: before reading a file or running a command, check whether its output is already in your context and reuse it; re-read only when it may have changed, and say why.
Rerun tests or builds only after the code changed or to get new evidence; save long output to a file and filter that instead of rerunning.
Revise an existing script instead of writing a near-copy; when repeated actions bring no new evidence, switch to a different approach.
```

The last three lines are `REUSE_RULES` (`CONTEXT_REUSE_RULES`, default `1`; `0` drops them and restores the earlier bytes). They condense the developer-designed skills of Hu et al., [Analyzing and Mitigating Cost-Inefficient Behaviors in Coding Agents](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.30725v1) (arXiv 2609.30725, §4.3 and Appendix A.4.2), whose seven rules include "Reuse Context … check whether it is already available in the current context. If yes, reuse it instead of fetching it again. Re-read only when necessary, and briefly state why", "Extract test signal precisely from a prior run instead of re-running the test. Only rerun if the source code has changed since the last run" and "Do not create numbered variants such as `repro2.py` or `fix_v3.py`; revise the original artifact". Preloaded into the system prompt, the full set cut cost 41.73% at +0.50 pp pass@1 for Mini-SWE-Agent with Sonnet 4.6 on 200 SWE-bench Verified tasks, 13.94% at −1.50 pp for Claude Code with Sonnet 4.6, and 16.03% at −2.17 pp for Mini-SWE-Agent with MiniMax-M3 (Table 3). No run of this proxy has measured them. The text names no tool, so it fits every harness; it is static and ends the instruction, so it adds no cache break of its own.

It is a constant (`STANDING_INSTRUCTION` in `proxy/smarter_compact/core.py` and `cli/coding-agent/context-trim.mjs`), so the system prefix is byte-identical on every request and the prompt cache keeps hitting. It is added after trimming: the cut, the token estimate and the fingerprint session id never see it. A request whose system text already contains it is left alone. `CONTEXT_STANDING_INSTRUCTION=0`, or `[context_proxy] standing_instruction = false` in config.toml, turns it off; `CONTEXT_PROXY_ENABLED=0` turns it off with the trim. Placement:

| Format | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Anthropic | One text block appended to `system`; a string `system` becomes a single leading text block first, an absent one becomes `[block]` |
| Chat | One `system` message inserted after the leading `system` / `developer` messages (index 0 when there are none) |
| Responses | Appended to `instructions` after a blank line (or set as `instructions` when absent). `instructions` precede every input item and stay fixed for a session, so a trim of `input` never moves the instruction |
| OpenCode 2 | One `{type: "text"}` entry pushed onto `event.system`, after the session banner |

Pointer note added at the cut turn after a trim ([note placement](#note-placement)):

```
[smarter-compact: continuing session <sid>; <n> earlier messages are NOT in your context. Older turns were moved out to save space, so a gap in what you see (missing batches, lines, keys) is in them. Continue the task from where you were. The tools smart_compact_search and smart_compact_sql are available to you in this request. You MUST call smart_compact_search(session_id="<sid>", query=... or pattern=...) before relying on anything in them, and never claim "not found", "never received" or "no search tool" without calling it. Dropped user turns may hold instructions or corrections that still apply: search them (smart_compact_search with role="user") before changing course. To recover a file you read earlier, search for the text you need instead of reading it again, and re-read only the lines you still lack (offset/limit). Every message of this session is stored and queryable with smart_compact_search and smart_compact_sql(session_id="<sid>", sql=...).]
```

It names no file path, so the proxy (in its container) and the OpenCode 2 plugin (on the host) produce the same bytes.

The block is computed once per cut and stored in the trim state, so later requests repeat it byte for byte. The OpenCode 2 plugin puts the wrapped block in its own text part, followed by a blank line; when OpenCode 2 compacts a session, the same block (unwrapped, without the blank line) becomes the compaction summary.

### Note placement

The trim note (pointer, clearing-only, reasoning-strip, with the scratchpad block ahead of it), the scratchpad nudge and the [ledger](clearing.md#ledger-context_ledger) block with its nudge lines are notes from the proxy, not the user. Where a note goes depends on what the client already sends:

| Request | Where the note goes |
| --- | --- |
| Holds a client system message after its first unpinned item (Claude Code: `<total_tokens>`, `# Environment`; Codex: `developer` items) | System-role text, unwrapped, after the run of user / tool items it belongs to (the cut turn for the trim note, the tool results for the ledger block, the newest item for the nudge). Anthropic adds it as text blocks at the end of the client's system message that already follows there, since two system messages may not be adjacent, else inserts `{"role": "system", "content": [text blocks]}`. Chat inserts `{"role": <the client's role>, "content": "<notes joined by a blank line>"}`; Responses inserts `{"type": "message", "role": <the client's role>, "content": [input_text parts]}` |
| No such message (and always in the OpenCode 2 / Pi plugin) | Inline, as before, wrapped the way Claude Code marks injected context: `<system-reminder>\n<note>\n</system-reminder>`. Anthropic: its own text block (first for the trim note, last for the others); Chat and Responses string content or output: after a blank line; plugin: its own text part, or after the tool result's text and a blank line |

The test is the client's own mid-conversation system message: it shows the route accepts one (Claude 4.8+ and the 5 family take the role; older Claude models reject it, and LiteLLM's OpenAI-shaped path places or converts it itself). OpenCode 2 drops system messages on some provider paths, so the plugin never uses the role.

A note is recorded state (trim state `note`, `nudge`, `ledger`), not client content: the client never stores it, the proxy renders it from that state on every request, so a note re-renders byte for byte until the next trim and is never written to `messages` rows. A note belongs to its anchor item: when a trim drops the anchor, the note goes with it, while client system messages stay pinned. A trim keeps only the newest ledger block and re-arms the nudge, as before. Tool-output placeholders (cleared, compressed, repeated-result and reuse pointers, input placeholders) replace the tool's own content and are never wrapped.

Compressed tool result:

```
[smarter-compact: tool result compressed, <tokens> tokens — smart_compact_get(id="<id>") returns the full text]
<head excerpt>
…
<tail excerpt>
```

The compressed form is a pure function of the original content and the configured thresholds, so the same tool result renders to the same bytes on every request and the prompt-cache prefix stays valid.

`scripts/tests/test_context_parity.mjs` runs the fixture requests in `scripts/tests/fixtures/context-parity.json` through both implementations and requires identical views, session database contents (every `messages` and `lines` column, `sqlite_master`, `user_version`) and blobs. The fixture also holds the golden standing instruction and pointer text, which `STANDING_INSTRUCTION` and `pointer_text` / `pointerText` must reproduce byte for byte.

# Smarter Compact **Context management (smart compaction) for coding agents.** Long sessions keep small, cached prompts. Every message goes into a local SQLite session store. Once the prompt reaches your token limit, older turns leave it, and the next kept turn carries a pointer to them.

On ContextBench with Haiku 5.5 it cost **85% less** than keeping everything, averaged over four task sizes, and scored higher on the log tasks. [Results](benchmarks.md). The agent searches the store with `smart_compact_search`, `smart_compact_sql`, and `smart_compact_get` when it needs a detail back. # OpenCode

The package default export provides `setup` (OpenCode 2 context hook and MCP self-registration) and `server` (OpenCode 1 headers and `/compact`).

## Install

OpenCode 2 (`opencode` >= 2.2):

```sh
opencode plugin add smarter-compact            # npm package (recommended)
opencode plugin add <user>/smarter-compact     # Git shorthand
opencode plugin list                            # installed package plugins
```

Both write `"plugins": ["<spec>"]` to the global config and install the package under the OpenCode npm cache.

From a local clone, `plugin add` accepts only npm/Git specs; point the config at the checkout instead:

```jsonc
{ "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/smarter-compact"] }
```

Keep the clone in place; OpenCode resolves the package from it.

## OpenCode 2

The plugin registers its context hooks by itself, and *attempts* to register its search MCP
tools the same way (`ctx.mcp.add`, OpenCode >= 2.2). OpenCode can accept that call and still
connect no server, so **write the `mcp` entry below as well** and rely on it. Registering twice
is harmless. Options are the same keys
as `CONTEXT_*` env vars (camelCase in JSON):

```jsonc
// opencode.json
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "smarter-compact",
      "options": {
        "trimAtTokens": 125000,
        "compressOverTokens": 4000
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

OpenCode 2 trims inside the plugin. You do not run `smarter-compact enable opencode` or point `provider.anthropic.options.baseURL` at the proxy.

Commands:

- `/compact` — trim on the next request (registered by the plugin).
- MCP tools `smart_compact_search`, `smart_compact_sql`, `smart_compact_get`, `context_status` (needs `node` >= 24 on `PATH`). Configure them explicitly — the plugin's own `ctx.mcp.add` is best effort:

```jsonc
// opencode.json — same store the plugin trims into, so $SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR must match
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "smarter-compact": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["node", "/path/to/smarter-compact/plugin/lib/mcp/server.mjs"],
        "environment": { "SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR": "/var/lib/smarter-compact" },
        "enabled": true
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Verify rather than assume: the plugin prints one `smarter-compact: recall MCP registered` (or
`NOT registered reason=…`) line to stderr at startup, and every answered call appends a line to
`$SMARTER_COMPACT_STATE_DIR/context/tool-calls.jsonl`. OpenCode exposes an MCP tool as
`<server>_<tool>` — `smarter-compact_smart_compact_search`, underscore, seen verbatim in captured
requests — so the pointer and standing instruction name that qualified form, never the bare one.

The scratchpad is on by default, and the nudge names `smarter-compact_smart_compact_scratchpad`. To turn it off, set `CONTEXT_SCRATCHPAD=0` in the server's `environment` too; the self-registration forwards it from the plugin's environment.
When a server is left behind code mode the tools are reachable only through that runner's
`execute` input, so counting top-level tool names alone under-reads recall to zero; the bench
therefore sets `"codemode": false` on this server.

## OpenCode 1

OpenCode 1 has no context hook, so trimming goes through the LiteLLM proxy:

```sh
./plugin/scripts/smarter-compact enable opencode
```

`enable` starts the proxy in the background (`CONTEXT_PROXY_PORT`, default 4101).

The proxy reads its own environment, so set `CONTEXT_*` variables or `proxy.env`; of the OpenCode 1 plugin options only `stateDir` applies, to session registration and `/compact` flags ([reference](configuration.md#opencode-plugin-options)).

The `server` hook sends `x-smarter-compact-session-id` when your Anthropic `baseURL` is the local proxy, registers the session, and honours `/compact`.
